idiom_name: Vitest/Jest describe + it with beforeEach and typed expect
implementation_notes: The skeleton is the JavaScript one - describe/it blocks, beforeEach hooks for the arrange beat, one act per test, expect matchers for the assert beat - but TypeScript adds two levers: Vitest's test.extend takes a typed fixture object (`base.extend<{ account: Account }>({ account: async ({}, use) => { await use(new Account(100)) } })`) rather than a fixture name and factory, and typed expect signatures can flag comparisons between unrelated types before the test runs. Jest with ts-jest or @swc/jest keeps the same API where the project already standardises on it, and expectTypeOf/assert<T>() serves genuinely type-level assertions.
pitfalls: A fixture factory that throws fails every test requesting it as a fixture error rather than an assertion, so a broken arrange beat reports once per test and masks the behaviour under test.
expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(Account) does not narrow the static type for later statements; add an explicit type guard when the assert beat needs typed access.
Test files are only type-checked when tsconfig's include/types cover them (or when vitest typecheck runs), so type errors in the assert beat otherwise surface at runtime only.
